messages.subject: Short summer SEM (and other) course(s) in Barcelona
parts:
Apologies for any cross-posting, but I teach a 3 half-day SEM course using lavaan for instruction.  If anyone (knows someone who) is interested, please find information and links below.

Thanks,
Terrence Jorgensen


Students, researchers and professionals can now register for Summer School courses, offered both online and in-person, by the Research and Expertise Centre for Survey Methodology (RECSM) at the University Pompeu Fabra, in Barcelona. Individuals who register for courses before the 28th of April will benefit from an early bird discount.

This is the 10th annual RECSM Summer School, taking place between June 26 - July 14 2023, and covering diverse topics on survey methodology and advanced statistical analysis of survey data.

The first week is composed of introductory courses including three on software programming in R, STATA & Python, while the second and third weeks take a more advanced approach to developing high quality surveys and employing more current and advanced statistical methods for the analysis of survey and other types of data. All are taught by experts in the respective subjects, many of them from various countries around the world.

Dates: June 26 to July 14, 2023 (see the course calendar for individual course dates)

Format: Online & On-site

Information: https://www.upf.edu/web/survey/summer-school-2023

Registration: https://eventum.upf.edu/93371/detail/recsm-summer-methods-school-2023.html

Contact: re...@upf.edu

I highly recommend this course, as I personally took it last year and found it to be exceptional. Prof. Jorgensen provides clear explanations and instructions, making it accessible to both beginners and those with prior knowledge. The course also encourages questions, so participants feel comfortable asking for clarification. Prof. Jorgensen has a talent for breaking down complex concepts into simple explanations, making the course easy to understand and follow. I would take it againanytime.

Thank you, prof. Jorgensen once again:)


Marina
